corridor_notes: P6229 = the 'Northern Xinjiang' (北疆) half of a 14-project, 4977 km strategic expansion announced 2023-07-08 by Xinjiang autonomous region government + PetroChina (5 northern projects / 2863.5 km / 4.66 billion RMB; 9 southern projects / 2113.5 km / 7.99 billion RMB = P6230). GEM's Wiki links this row to 'Zungharia Basin Rim Gas Pipeline Network' (准噶尔盆地周边天然气管网), consistent with what was found: a Karamay/Xinjiang-Oilfield hub (Jinlong Town + Karamay First Station, FuelSource = Karamay Oil Field) feeding gas 'benefit-the-people' (利民) branch pipelines that fan out to four northern prefectures — Tacheng, Altay, Ili (Yining), and Bortala (Bole) — plus a Karamay-to-Urumqi (Wangjiagou/Toutunhe) trunk, which matches GEM's existing StartLocation='Jinlong Town'/EndLocation='Wangjiagou' pair (both independently corroborated: Jinlong Town via a 2026 valve-well bidding notice at 'Jinlong Town First Station' in Karamay; Wangjiagou via CNPC Xinjiang Oilfield's registered 'Wangjiagou Oil & Gas Storage and Transport Center' in Urumqi's Toutunhe District). Altay and Bortala branches are each being built in two phases/segments (Kelamaili-Fuhai then Fuhai-Fuyun; Jinghe-Alashankou and Bole-Wenquan respectively), which is why their 'start'/'end' fields above span the full multi-phase corridor rather than a single short segment. Individual per-branch lengths as reported (Tacheng ~264-407 km depending on trunk-vs-trunk+branches count; Altay 246 km + 335.7 km; Bortala ~179-198 km combined) do not cleanly sum to the GEM total of 2863.5 km — this program is still under active construction/tendering as of mid-2026 and press figures for the same corridor vary by report date and by whether branch spurs are included.
researcher_notes: Strong MULTI_BRANCH result: 5 distinct legs sourced, 4 of them (Tacheng, Altay, Ili, Bortala) from official Xinjiang prefecture/autonomous-region government (.gov.cn) sites or Xinhua/state media, plus the Karamay-Wangjiagou trunk independently corroborating GEM's own pre-existing StartLocation/EndLocation. The 2023-07-08 ts.cn announcement article (already GEM's own Status/Proposal ref) is bot-walled (returns a bot-detection JS challenge page, HTTP 200, to both curl and the verifier) and has no Wayback snapshot — its '北疆5个项目/南疆9个项目' figures were confirmed instead via a search-engine cached snippet and independently via chinagas.org.cn / xjdrc.xinjiang.gov.cn coverage of the same figures, so I'm treating the underlying facts as corroborated even though ts.cn itself can't be verified live. No official single-document 'list of 5 named branches' was found; the branch roster here was assembled by cross-referencing prefecture-level progress reports (each explicitly described as part of 南北疆天然气利民管道扩建工程, the parent program) against GEM's own StartLocation/EndLocation and the 2023 north/south split. Karamay-based sources consistently reference TWO similarly-spelled-in-pinyin-but-distinct places: 克拉玛依/Karamay (the city/oilfield) vs 克拉美丽/Kelamaili (a gas field further east/northeast, in Altay-prefecture territory near Fuhai) — do not conflate them when drawing candidate geometry.
blockers: Could not find a single official document enumerating all 5 branches by name/length/exact endpoint in one place — figures were cross-referenced across multiple prefecture-level progress articles instead. Exact km figure for each branch varies by article/date because these are multi-phase, still-under-construction projects (as of 2026); no branch-by-branch length breakdown that sums cleanly to 2863.5 km was found. The Ili branch's two named sub-branches (Nilka vs Xinyuan) were not separately geocoded with distinct endpoints — only the shared Yining hub and Nilka (as one representative distal point) were sourced with confidence.
